name: Varunprasaath R. Selvaraju, Ph.D.
summary: PhD analytical/materials chemist with 6+ years in multi-technique characterization, method-development documentation, stability/degradation analysis, and DOE/QbD-style process readouts. Brings separations-science exposure (GPC/SEC, LC-MS-adjacent workflows) and technical-report depth to analytical method development while bridging honestly into biologics-specific platforms.

education.details: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (Top 1% nationally)

bullets: Lead DOE-guided analytical readout design for bio-based polymer process development, defining process windows, reproducibility criteria, and SOP-ready specifications.
Connect FT-IR, thermal-analysis, spectroscopy, and process data to stability interpretation, troubleshooting, and technical recommendations.
Characterized 15+ functional material variants using UV-Vis-NIR, FT-IR, cyclic voltammetry, spectroelectrochemistry, NMR, GPC/SEC, TGA, DSC, and MS-informed analysis.
Mapped degradation and stability failure modes through hypothesis-driven experiments, orthogonal characterization, structured datasets, and publication-quality technical documentation.
Developed molecular thin-film coating processes and linked CVD/surface-preparation variables with morphology, interface quality, and material performance.
Optimized CVD polymer thin-film deposition with DOE strategies and in-situ QCM-D monitoring to quantify growth kinetics and improve reproducibility.

Managed characterization/process-development lab operations for a 15-member group; implemented equipment tracking, calibration routines, SOPs, and safety protocols that improved instrument uptime by 30% and strengthened data integrity.
